content.value_statement: Finding a domain name is slow when good ideas are already taken. This skill generates brandable options, compares TLD choices, and helps organize availability checks.
actual_capabilities: Generates domain name ideas from a project description and target audience.
Organizes suggestions across TLDs such as .com, .io, .dev, .ai, and .app.
Explains why each name may fit the brand, audience, or product category.
Suggests variations when preferred names are unavailable, expensive, or too generic.
Provides naming tips, registration priorities, and follow-up brand checks.
limitations: Availability and pricing can change quickly and need live registrar confirmation.
It does not perform legal trademark clearance.
It cannot guarantee social handle availability without checking each platform.
Quality depends on accurate project, audience, and naming preference details.

use_cases.title: Name a New Startup
use_cases.description: Generate a shortlist of brandable domains that match a business idea, audience, and preferred TLDs.

use_cases.title: Explore Product Rebrand Options
use_cases.description: Compare naming directions, keyword themes, and domain extensions before choosing a new product identity.

use_cases.title: Find a Personal Brand Domain
use_cases.description: Create portfolio or creator domain options using a name, profession, niche, and preferred tone.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Starter Names
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [project description] for [target audience]. Brainstorm domain name ideas across .com, .io, and .app. Explain why each name works.

prompt_templates.title: Use Keywords and TLDs
prompt_templates.prompt: Brainstorm domain names for [project]. Use the keywords [keyword list] when useful. Prioritize short names and include .com, .dev, and .ai options.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Brand Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these domain name ideas: [domain list]. Rank them by memorability, clarity, pronunciation, audience fit, and likely availability concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Naming Strategy Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a domain naming strategy for [business or product]. Include naming themes, TLD tradeoffs, fallback variations, registration priorities, social handle checks, and trademark review reminders.

output_examples.input: I am building a collaboration tool for remote design teams.
output: Recommended direction: short names that suggest flow, shared space, and creative review.
Example shortlist: StudioRelay, CanvasCrew, DesignHarbor, ReviewNest, and PixelSync.
Next checks: registrar availability, similar trademarks, social handles, and confusing competitor names.

output_examples.input: Suggest names for an AI budgeting app with .ai or .app options.
output: Recommended direction: names that combine money clarity with helpful automation.
Example shortlist: BudgetPilot, Spendwise, CashCue, WalletGuide, and PennyPath.
TLD note: .app supports a consumer product feel, while .ai signals the assistant feature more directly.

output_examples.input: Compare my shortlist: taskforge.com, sprintnest.io, and backlogbee.dev.
output: Best brand fit: SprintNest, because it is short, team-oriented, and easy to say.
Highest clarity: TaskForge, because it directly signals work creation and project execution.
Main concern: BacklogBee may feel playful, so confirm that tone matches the product audience.

best_practices: Provide the project purpose, audience, tone, and competitors before asking for names.
Specify preferred TLDs, maximum length, keywords, and words to avoid.
Confirm registrar availability, pricing, trademarks, and social handles before buying.
anti_patterns: Asking for one perfect name without project context or naming constraints.
Treating generated availability notes as final without a live registrar check.
Choosing names that are hard to spell, pronounce, or distinguish from existing brands.

faq.question: Does this skill register domains?
faq.answer: No. It helps brainstorm and evaluate names, but registration must happen through a domain registrar.

faq.question: Can it verify live availability?
faq.answer: It can organize availability checks and summarize results when tools or user-provided data are available. Always confirm with a registrar.

faq.question: Can it help with personal brand domains?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide your name, profession, audience, and preferred tone for tailored portfolio or creator domain ideas.

faq.question: Does it replace trademark review?
faq.answer: No. It can remind you to check trademarks, but legal review requires qualified trademark research.

faq.question: What information improves the suggestions?
faq.answer: Share the product category, target audience, brand tone, keywords, competitor names, and TLD preferences.
